exercise.name: Seated Hammer Curl
library_steps: Sit tall on a bench, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing in.
Curl both dumbbells up with your thumbs on top.
Lower them slowly until your arms hang straight.
exercise.one_line_summary: Sitting tall on an upright bench, arms hanging beside the seat with palms facing in; curl both dumbbells (thumbs up) to ~125 deg elbow bend with the upper arms still by the sides. Elbow flexors (biceps, brachialis) work; brachioradialis/forearm helps.

setup.target: Upright bench (back pad ~85 deg), sit tall, feet flat and wider than hips.
setup.why: Seated removes leg drive and hip swing.

setup.target: Hang by the sides, parallel to the trunk, and stay there.
setup.why: EMG protocol kept the arms parallel to the trunk with no humeral flexion.

setup.target: Neutral: palms face the body, thumbs forward at the bottom and up at the top.

movement.end: 125 deg (dumbbell near the shoulder, not touching)

movement.measure: upper arm angle from the torso side

muscles.emg: Neutral grip curl: biceps 12 +- 9% lower than supinated in the lifting phase, still a main mover (S1).
Neutral grip 6 +- 5% lower than supinated (S1) - the popular 'more brachioradialis' claim was not confirmed.
not measured by surface EMG; deep elbow flexor
9 +- 2% higher with neutral than supinated grip (S1), steadying the humeral head.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Upper arms rise to the front as the dumbbells come up.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Front delt lifts the weight; studies fixed the arm by the trunk.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Thumbs rotate out at the top.

sources.citation: Coratella G, Tornatore G, Longo S, Toninelli N, Padovan R, Esposito F, Ce E. 2023. Biceps brachii and brachioradialis excitation in biceps curl exercise: different handgrips, different synergy. Sports (Basel) 11(3):64.
sources.what_it_gave: n=10 bodybuilders, 8RM, standing, arms parallel to the trunk with no humeral flexion, 1-2-1-2 s. Supinated > neutral for biceps (+12%) and brachioradialis (+6%); neutral > supinated for front delt (+9%).

sources.citation: Oliveira LF, Matta TT, Alves DS, Garcia MAC, Vieira TMM. 2009. Effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls. J Sports Sci Med 8:24-29.
sources.what_it_gave: Arms-alongside-the-body curl: biceps activity rises toward the top third of the range; elbow range ~115-132 deg; reps started at ~20 deg flexion.

clip_check.check: Start: arms hanging, elbow ~5 deg, dumbbells beside the seat (not in it)
End: elbow 125 deg, upper arm still by the side
Biceps strongest red in both pictures
